# **CS355 Mini-Project**

# **Abhay Rathour \- 1901CS77**

**![][image1]**

**Task A: Guest House Related Service**

We were required to create guest house module in our mini project which was capable of doing the following tasks: \-

* Monthly bookings for the guest house in different categories   
* The total monthly expenditure for the guest house  
* Generation of bills  
* Availability of room  
* Monthly food billing

**E-R Model**

![][image2]

The relationships are described as follows:

* Guest House Duty \- Relates that due to booking of a guest, a staff member is assigned a duty. Only one staff member can be assigned duty for a booking by a guest, so it is a one-to-many relationship with staff at one end.  
* Pays \- Guests make a payment for bookings.  
* Books \- Guest books accommodation, rooms and food.  
* Menu bill \- Food order creates a bill for the restaurant.  
* Options \- Room and accommodation bookings have different options to choose from which depend upon the status if they are available or not.

**Relational Model**

**![][image3]**

**Primary key**

Primary key is given in blue.

AID, SID, GID, RID, FID are the primary keys for their tables.

**Foreign key**

Foreign key is given in orange.

Staff can be assigned a duty only when it is in the staff table.

A guest can order food and make payment only when it is in the guest table.

A room can be booked only when the guest is in guest table and room is in optionsr table.

The Tables are optimised as we can see.

They are in 1NF as all values in all tables are atomic.

They are also optimised to be in 2NF form.

They are in 3NF form as there is no transitive partial dependency for non-prime attributes in the tables

They are also in BCNF as for every attribute it is only dependent on the primary key and Hence all LHS of Functional dependency will be SuperKey.

**Queries**

Create database

DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS guesthouse;

CREATE DATABASE guesthouse;

USE guesthouse;

Create tables

* Guest \- Stores data about the guests which register on the site and use the portal to do the bookings.

CREATE TABLE \`guest\` (  
  \`gid\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`name\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`age\` int(11) NOT NULL,  
  \`phoneNo\` int(11) NOT NULL,  
  \`password\` varchar(100) NOT NULL  
);

ALTER TABLE \`guest\`  
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (\`gid\`);

* Accommodation \- Stores data about taxi bookings like ids of guest, taxi, driver and date.

CREATE TABLE \`Accomodation\` (  
  \`AID\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`GID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`SID\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`accomodationDate\` date DEFAULT NULL  
);

* Dutyschedule \- Stores data about duty schedule of the staff.

CREATE TABLE \`dutySchedule\` (  
  \`sid\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`date\` date NOT NULL,  
  \`wage\` int(11) NOT NULL  
);

* Menu \- Stores data about menu items for the food booking.

CREATE TABLE \`menu\` (  
  \`fid\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`name\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`description\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`price\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL  
);

ALTER TABLE \`menu\`  
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (\`fid\`);

* Payment \- Stores bill due for a guest.

CREATE TABLE \`payment\` (  
  \`GID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`date\` date DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`totalBill\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL  
);

ALTER TABLE \`payment\`  
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (\`GID\`);

* resourceStatus \- Stores the availability of a resource.

CREATE TABLE \`resourceStatus\` (  
  \`ID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`Date\` date DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`isAvailable\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL  
);

* restaurant \- Stores the data about food orders of a guest.

CREATE TABLE \`restaurant\` (  
  \`gid\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`date\` date NOT NULL,  
  \`bill\` int(11) NOT NULL  
);

* Room \- Stores data about room booking of a guest.

CREATE TABLE \`Room\` (  
  \`RID\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`GID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`date\` date NOT NULL,  
  \`bill\` int(11) NOT NULL  
);

* Staff \- Stores all the data about the staff.

CREATE TABLE \`staff\` (  
  \`SID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`Name\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`Age\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`PhoneNo\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`Department\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`Role\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`password\` varchar(100) NOT NULL  
);

ALTER TABLE \`staff\`  
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (\`SID\`);

* OptionsA \- Stores data of the transport services.

CREATE TABLE \`optionsA\` (  
  \`AID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`carName\` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`description\` varchar(500) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`price\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL  
);

ALTER TABLE \`optionsA\`  
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (\`AID\`);

* OptionsR \- Stores data about the rooms.

CREATE TABLE \`optionsR\` (  
  \`RID\` varchar(100) NOT NULL,  
  \`description\` varchar(500) DEFAULT NULL,  
  \`price\` int(11) DEFAULT NULL  
);

ALTER TABLE \`optionsR\`  
  ADD PRIMARY KEY (\`RID\`);

* Login for guest

// Guest login  
    if (isset($\_POST\['login\_user'\])) {

        // storing input from user in variables  
        $username \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['gid'\]);  
        $password \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['password'\]);

        // neither of fields should be empty  
        if (empty($username)) {  
            array\_push($errors, "Guest ID is required.");  
        }  
        if (empty($password)) {  
            array\_push($errors, "Password is required.");  
        }  
         
        if (count($errors) \== 0) {  
            $query \= "SELECT \* FROM guest WHERE GID \= '$username' AND password \= '$password' ";  
            $results \= mysqli\_query($db, $query);  
                 
            if (mysqli\_num\_rows($results) \== 1) {  
                $row \= mysqli\_fetch\_assoc($results);

                // store guest data in SESSION for further use  
                $\_SESSION\['username'\] \= $username;  
                $\_SESSION\['Guestname'\] \= $row\["name"\];  
                $\_SESSION\['GuestmobileNumber'\] \= $row\["phoneNo"\];  
                $\_SESSION\['Guestage'\] \= $row\["age"\];  
                $\_SESSION\['GuestPassword'\] \= $row\["password"\];  
                 
                $\_SESSION\['success'\] \= "Successfully logged in\!";  
                header('location: GuestInfo.php');  
            } else {  
                array\_push($errors, "Wrong username/password combination.");  
            }  
        }  
    }

* Updating the tables when a booking is made

// Post-payment updation of tables  
    if (isset($\_POST\['payIt'\])) {  
        $gid \= $\_SESSION\['username'\];

        $name \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['name'\]);  
        $phoneNo \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['phoneNo'\]);  
        $username \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['username'\]);  
        $cardname \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['cardname'\]);  
        $cardnumber \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['cardnumber'\]);  
        $expmonth \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['expmonth'\]);  
        $expyear \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['expyear'\]);  
        $cvv \= mysqli\_real\_escape\_string($db, $\_POST\['cvv'\]);

        $query \= "SELECT \* FROM guest WHERE gid \= '$gid'";  
        $row \= mysqli\_fetch\_assoc(mysqli\_query($db, $query));

        if ($username \!== $gid) {  
            array\_push($errors, "Guest ID does not match");  
        }

        date\_default\_timezone\_set('Asia/Kolkata');  
        $timezone \= date('Y-m-d');  
         
        $year \= date('Y', strtotime($timezone));  
        $month \= date('F', strtotime($timezone));  
         
        if ($expmonth \!== "January"  &&  
            $expmonth \!== "February" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "March" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "April" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "May" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "June" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "July" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "August" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "September" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "October" &&  
            $expmonth \!== "November"  &&  
            $expmonth \!== "December") {  
            array\_push($errors, "Please enter valid Expiry Month");  
        }

        if ($expyear \< $year) {  
            array\_push($errors, "Card has expired");  
        } elseif ($expyear \=== $year && $month \< $expmonth) {  
            array\_push($errors, "Card has expired");  
        }

        if (count($errors)==0) {  
            $bill \= $\_SESSION\['bill'\];  
            $check \= mysqli\_query($db, "SELECT \* FROM payment WHERE gid \= '$gid' ");  
             
            if (mysqli\_num\_rows($check) \== 1) {  
                $update\_ \= "UPDATE payment SET totalbill \= totalbill \+ '$bill', date \= '$timezone' WHERE gid \= '$gid' ";  
                $row \= mysqli\_query($db, $update\_);  
            } else {  
                $insert \= "INSERT INTO payment (GID, date, totalBill) VALUES ('$gid', '$timezone', '$bill')";  
                $check \= mysqli\_query($db, $insert);  
            }

            if($\_SESSION\['what'\] \=== "restaurant"){  
               $insert \= "INSERT INTO restaurant (gid, date, bill) VALUES ('$gid', '$timezone', '$bill')";  
               mysqli\_query($db, $insert);

               $staff \= "INSERT INTO dutySchecule (sid, date, wage) VALUES ('S3', '$timezone', 50)";  
               mysqli\_query($db, $staff);

               $staff\_ \= "INSERT INTO dutySchecule (sid, date, wage) VALUES ('S1', '$timezone', 200)";  
               mysqli\_query($db, $staff\_);  
            }  
            else if($\_SESSION\['what'\] \== "room") {  
               $rid \= $\_SESSION\['Roomrid'\];  
               $date1 \= $\_SESSION\['startDateRoom'\];  
               $date2 \= $\_SESSION\['endDateRoom'\];

               $insert \= "INSERT INTO Room (rid, gid, date, bill) VALUES ('$rid', '$gid', '$timezone', '$bill')";  
               $B \= mysqli\_query($db, $insert);

               $diff \= abs(strtotime($date2) \- strtotime($date1));  
               $years \= floor($diff / (365\*60\*60\*24));  
               $months \= floor(($diff \- $years \* 365\*60\*60\*24) / (30\*60\*60\*24));  
               $days \= floor(($diff \- $years \* 365\*60\*60\*24 \- $months\*30\*60\*60\*24)/ (60\*60\*24));  
                 
                while($days\--) {  
                    echo $date1;  
                    echo " ";  
                        $insert\_ \= "INSERT INTO resourceStatus (id, date, isAvailable) VALUES ('$rid','$date1', 0)";  
                        $date1 \= date('Y-m-d', strtotime("+1 day", strtotime($date1)));  
                        $A \= mysqli\_query($db, $insert\_ );  
                }

                $staff \= "INSERT INTO dutySchecule (sid, date, wage) VALUES ('S6', '$timezone', 100)";  
                mysqli\_query($db, $staff);  
            }  
            else if($\_SESSION\['what'\] \== "accomodation") {  
                $order \= $\_SESSION\['Cardate'\];  
                $aid \= $\_SESSION\['Caraid'\];

                $insert \= "INSERT INTO Accomodation (aid, gid, sid, accomodationDate) VALUES ('$aid', '$gid', 'S4', '$order')";  
                $B \= mysqli\_query($db, $insert);

                $insert\_ \= "INSERT INTO resourceStatus (id, date, isAvailable) VALUES ('$aid','$order', 0)";  
                $A \= mysqli\_query($db, $insert\_ );

                $staff \= "INSERT INTO dutySchecule (sid, date, wage) VALUES ('S4', '$order', 1000)";  
                mysqli\_query($db, $staff);  
            }

            header('location: confirmation.php');  
        }

**Task B: Market Shop Related Services**

 **ER Diagram:**

**![][image17]**

**·        Shop relation contains information about different shops on the campus.**

**·        Shopkeeper relation contains details about the Shopkeepers of different Shops.**

**·        Gatepass relation contains information about gatepass validity of campus visitors.**

**·        Feedback relation contains feedback of different shops from students on the basis of parameters like Product/Service quality, Shopkeeper behaviour, Value for money, Variety available. These parameters are rated from 1 to 10 by the students who are identified by unique Roll Numbers.**

**·        BillDetails relation contains monthly bills (Electricity Bill and Shop Rent) for each shop.**

**·        PayDetails relation contains details of payments from each Shop.**

**·        PendingCharges relation contains the pending charges (Electricity Bill and Shop Rent) from each Shop.**

**·        License relationship links shopkeepers to their shops along with their license period.**

**·        One shop can have many feedback(from different students), one shop can have many bill details(bills for different months), one shop can have many pay details, one shop can have many shopkeepers, one shopkeeper has one gatepass and one shop has one record for pending charges.**

**Relational Schema:**

**![][image18]**

**·        Primary keys are underlined.**

**·        Shop\_ID, Shopkeeper\_ID, Gatepass\_ID , (Shop\_ID, Shopkeeper\_ID), FID, PID, Bill\_ID, Reference\_ID uniquely identifies each record in their respective tables hence are defined primary keys.**

**·        Foreign keys are indicated by arrows.**

**·        Shop\_ID can be a part of Feedback, License, BillDetails, PayDetails and PendingCharges if and only if it is present in Shop relation hence the foreign keys are defined. Also, the relation License links Shopkeepers to their shops so the Shopkeeper\_IDs in License relation must be present in Shopkeeper relation, hence the foreign key is defined.**

**TASK C: \- Landscaping Related Activities**  
We were required to create a module in our mini project which was capable of doing the following tasks: \-

* Maintaining gardeners details  
* Identifying campus areas,   
* Gardeners assignments,   
* Duty roster(Monthly),   
* Equipment stock and maintenance details,   
* Handling grass cutting requests  
    
1) Entity-Relation Model for A database capable of doing above mentioned tasks: \-  
     
   ![][image47]  
     
     
   In the above ER Diagram some special points are as follows: \-  
1. Gardeners Entity has 1 multivalued attribute At\_Date which stores that specific gardener’s attendance. In the relational model, I have stored it in a different table.  
2. Relationship “ Assigned At” relates that a given gardener with ID GID is assigned at area with given AreaCode.

   Since multiple gardeners can be assigned to the same area and A gardener can work on multiple areas, it is a Many to Many Relationship.

3. Relationship “Has Equipment” relates 1 area with all the equipment that given area has. Since each equipment belongs to a single area it is a one to many relationship.  
4. Relationship “GCRequest At” related Grass Cutting Request to its area it is from, so each request belongs to a single area but A single area can have many requests, so it is many to 1 relationship.  
5. Relationship “Went for Maintenance” Relates equipment to its maintenance log, since each equipment can be sent for maintenance multiple times it is a one to many relationship.  
6. Admins entity is not related to any other Entity as it just stores login username and password for Administrator accounts(supervisors).  
     
2)  Relational Model : \-  
    ![][image48]  
     
   Primary Keys for Relationship Tables: \-  
   	Attendance: \-  GID+ At\_Date  
   	DutyAssignment: \- 	GID \+ Wday  
   	  
   For all other tables, Primary Key is in blue colour and foreign Keys are in green.  
     
   The Tables are optimised as we can see.  
   They are  in 1NF as all values in all tables are atomic.  
   They are also optimised to be in 2NF form.  
   They are in  3NF form as there is no transitive partial dependency for non-prime attributes in the tables  
   They are also in BCNF as for every attribute it is only dependent on the primary key and Hence all LHS of Functional dependency will be SuperKey.

3\) Queries to Create and populate above relational schema in our mysql Server: \- 

| $ mysql \-u root \- p |
| :---- |

	  
**QUERIES: \-**  
	Create Database and Use it: \-

| 	 \>	CREATE DATABASE Landscaping;	 \>	USE Landscaping;	 \>	GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON Landscaping.\* TO 'scot'@'localhost'; |
| :---- |

	  
	Creating all required tables: \-

1.  **Gardeners Table :**  This table stores all the gardener details like :gardener ID, name, address, contactNo, allotted holiday in week (0-6) ,date of employment etc.

   QUERY: \-

| \> CREATE TABLE Gardeners (  GID char(5) PRIMARY KEY,  GardenerName varchar(30) NOT NULL,  passwd varchar(255) ,  ContactNo char(10) ,  Address varchar(45) ,  DoE date NOT NULL,  Holiday int ); |
| :---- |
|  |

   

2.  **Attendance Table :** this stores GID of gardeners paired with dates they were present at.  
   	QUERY: \- 

   \> **CREATE** **TABLE** Attendance (  
     GID char(5) **NOT** NULL,  
     At\_Date datetime **NOT** NULL,  
     PRIMARY **KEY** (GID,At\_Date),  
     **CONSTRAINT** fk\_Attendance\_1 FOREIGN **KEY** (GID) **REFERENCES**    Gardeners (GID\> **CREATE** **TABLE** DutyAssignment (  
     GID char(5) **NOT** NULL,  
     AreaCode int **NOT** NULL,  
     Wday int **NOT** NULL,  
     PRIMARY **KEY** (GID,Wday),  
     **KEY** fk\_DutyAssignment\_2\_idx (AreaCode),  
     **CONSTRAINT** fk\_DutyAssignment\_1 FOREIGN **KEY** (GID) **REFERENCES** Gardeners (GID),  
     **CONSTRAINT** fk\_DutyAssignment\_2 FOREIGN **KEY** (AreaCode) **REFERENCES** Areas (AreaCode)  
   );

     
3. **DutyAssignment Table:**  This relation stores the tuples(Wday (weekday), GID, AreaCode) which represent that on a given weekday , gardener with GID works in  Area with this AreaCode.

            QUERY: \-

| \> CREATE TABLE DutyAssignment (  GID char(5) NOT NULL,  AreaCode int NOT NULL,  Wday int NOT NULL,  PRIMARY KEY (GID,Wday),  KEY fk\_DutyAssignment\_2\_idx (AreaCode),  CONSTRAINT fk\_DutyAssignment\_1 FOREIGN KEY (GID) REFERENCES Gardeners (GID),  CONSTRAINT fk\_DutyAssignment\_2 FOREIGN KEY (AreaCode) REFERENCES Areas (AreaCode)); |
| :---- |

4. **Areas Table :**  This table stores details about how campus is divided into different areas.

            QUERY: \-

| \> CREATE TABLE Areas (  AreaCode int PRIMARY KEY,  AreaName varchar(30) NOT NULL,  AreaLocation varchar(45) NOT NULL,); |
| :---- |

5. **GCRequests Table:** This table stores the various grass cutting requests submitted by employees or other officials residing on campus.  
   QUERY: \-

| \> CREATE TABLE GCRequests (  ReqID int  AUTO\_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,  AreaCode int NOT NULL,  ReqEmpID varchar(30) NOT NULL,  ReqContact char(10) NOT NULL,  ReqStatus varchar(15),  KEY fk\_GCRequests\_1\_idx (AreaCode),  CONSTRAINT fk\_GCRequests\_1 FOREIGN KEY (AreaCode) REFERENCES Areas(AreaCode)); |
| :---- |

   

6. **Equipments Relation:** This relation stores all the currently available equipment and tools on campus and their allotted areas.

QUERY: \-	

| \> CREATE TABLE Equipments (  		   EID char(5) PRIMARY KEY,    Area int NOT NULL,  		    EquipmentName varchar(15) NOT NULL,  		    KEY fk\_Equipments\_1\_idx (Area), 		    CONSTRAINT fk\_Equipments\_1 FOREIGN KEY (Area)     REFERENCES Areas (AreaCode)); |
| :---- |

7. **EqMaintenance Relation :-** This relation stores maintenance logs for equipment who have gone for repairing or maintenance.

QUERY: \-

| \> CREATE TABLE EqMaintenance (  ReqID int  AUTO\_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,  EID char(5) NOT NULL,  MDate date NOT NULL,  MPlace varchar(45) NOT NULL,  MContact char(10) NOT NULL,  MStatus varchar(10) NULL,  KEY fk\_EqMaintenance\_1\_idx (EID),  CONSTRAINT fk\_EqMaintenance\_1 FOREIGN KEY (EID) REFERENCES Equipments (EID)); |
| :---- |

8. **Admins Table:** This simply stores the username and password for admin accounts registered through the portal.

QUERY: \-

| \> CREATE TABLE \`Admins\` (  username varchar(20) PRIMARY KEY,  passwd varchar(255) NOT NULL,  isAdmin tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',); |
| :---- |

	isAdmin is made 1 by another admin after verification. Admin accounts are useless unless they are verified and made active by another Administrator. First account is made administrator manually through sql query.

**4\) QUERIES (php-mysql) for required tasks used in web interface: \-**  
All following queries have php variables after proper validation and after converting into mysql escape sequence to protect from sql injection attacks.

1) **Registration for Admin Account: \-**

| $query= "INSERT INTO Admins(username,passwd) VALUES ('$username','$hashed\_password')";if ($result \= mysqli\_query($db,$query)){    echo "\<script\>alert('Successfully Registered. Please Login\!'); window.location.href='./adminLogin.php';\</script\>"; } |

2) **Login for Admin : \-**

	

| $query="SELECT \* FROM Admins WHERE username='$username'";           if ($result \= mysqli\_query($db,$query)) {               $nr=mysqli\_num\_rows($result);               if($nr==0)                   $err="This User does not exist.Please enter correct Username.";               else               {                      $row=mysqli\_fetch\_array($result);                       $hashed\_password= $row\['passwd'\];                       if(password\_verify($passwd, $hashed\_password))                       {                           session\_start();                           $\_SESSION\["username"\] \= $username;                           $\_SESSION\["loggedin"\] \= true;                           $\_SESSION\["admin"\]=$row\['isAdmin'\];                           *//Redirect user to welcome page*                           echo "Login Successful\!";                           header("location: adminWelcome.php");                        }                       else{                           $err="Incorrect credentials given.";                       }  }   } |

**4\. Web Interface for this mini-project: \-**  
   
	I created the following pages to interact with the database designed above.

1. Homepage: This page takes you to either Administrator section, Gardener section or Grass cutting req portal.  
   ![][image49]  
2. When we click on the Gardener button, we go into the gardener section where we can register and then login.  
   ![][image50]  
3. Clicking on the Register button sends us to the register page where we register gardnerID and create password for login.

	![][image51]  
	

4. Let's fill it with gardenerID “BH001” and create a password and submit. We get redirected to the login page if registration is successful.  
   ![][image52]  
5. After filling “BH001” and the password we created we can login into the gardener’s profile page.

	![][image53]

6. We can click on update contact number to update gardener’s contact no, clicking on Area division shows us how campus is divided into various areas and view schedule displays Gardener’s work schedule.  
   ![][image54]      
   Schedule:

![][image55]

Campus Areas:   
![][image56]

7. Lets log out and check out grass cutting request system : \-  
   	![][image57]  
8. We can use submit New Req button to submit a new request.  
   ![][image58]  
   	Lets submit a req by empID: 1901CS77 for AreaCode 5 with a random contactNo.  
   	  
9. After successful submission we are redirected to request’s section where we can see our new request.  
   ![][image59]

Administrators can login and update status once request is fulfilled.

10. Now coming back to the homepage when we click for Admin Section, we can register for an admin account or login, Registration only generates a username and password but we cannot use it to login unless it is authorised by another Admin.

	Admin Section Homepage: \-  
	![][image60]  
	Admin account register form: \-  
	![][image61]  
	After filling in and once our account is authorised we can login using this username password. For further tasks let's use an already authorised account username” abhay376” and password ”12345678”.  
	Login Page: \-  
	![][image62]  
	After successful login we are sent to our welcome page where we get various functionalities.  
	![][image63]  
i) Make an admin: this button opens up a form where we can fill in a username to authorise admin access.  
	![][image64]  
ii)Gardener Details: This button lists out all gardener’s details currently employed.  
	![][image65]  
iii) clicking Insert new gardener opens up a form where we can fill in another record for any new gardener in the database.  
![][image66]  
iv) another button on adminwelcome page is Attendance, where we can mark attendance for any given GID. We cannot choose date for security purposes, it automatically takes in the current server date.  
	![][image67]  
	From here we can also see our monthly attendance for any specific month.  
	![][image68]  
v) Next button on the homepage is for maintenance of equipment records.  
	When we click on it, we can see the current stock of equipment and tools and we also get a form to add a new one.  
![][image69]  
vi) After clicking view maintenance status, we can also see the current maintenance log, insert a new value or update status of old log.  
![][image70]  
Status Update Form: \-  
![][image71]  
vii) Similarly heading to next section Grass Cutting req, as an Admin we get to see a new button to update status of req if it has been fulfilled.  
	![][image72]  
viii) Last button other than logout in our Admin homepage is for schedule.  
	Clicking this button opens up a form where we can fill our desired day to get a list of available gardeners for scheduling on that day and we can assign them any area code of our choice.  
	![][image73]  
Here let's assign Area 5 to BH003 on day4 i.e. Wednesday.  
Then we can click on current schedule to see updated Schedule: \-  
	![][image74]  
viii) After Logout we return to our mainpage index.php
